topic: The points requirement is a result, not a rule
text:
Irish course requirements are quoted as points — 520 for one course, 430 for another — and they read like thresholds set by the university. They are not. Each figure is simply the score of the lowest-scoring applicant admitted the previous year, so it describes last year’s demand rather than this year’s standard.

The practical consequences run both ways. A course whose points jumped last year may settle back. A course that looks comfortably within reach may rise. And a student a few points short of last year’s figure has not been told no by anyone — nobody has set that bar, and this year’s will be wherever the applicants put it.
attribution: How CAO points requirements are generated, as described by CAO and the institutions
whatThisIsNot: Not a suggestion that points are negotiable or that a place can be argued for. The allocation itself is strictly mechanical.
